react.note: React itself: components, props, state and hooks

react-native.note: The framework: turns React components into real iOS/Android views

@react-native/new-app-screen.note: The template's welcome screen; remove it when you build your own UI

expo.note: The Expo SDK: its version decides which React Native and expo-* versions fit (`npx expo install` picks them)

react-dom.note: React for web browsers; used when the app also runs on the web

react-native-web.note: Runs React Native components in a web browser (`npx expo start --web`)

react-native-nitro-modules.note: Fast native modules framework; needed by libraries built with Nitro (like MMKV 3+)

@react-navigation/native.note: Core of React Navigation: NavigationContainer and navigation hooks

@react-navigation/native-stack.note: Stack navigator using native screens (push/pop with a back button)

@react-navigation/stack.note: Stack navigator written in JavaScript (more customizable animations)

@react-navigation/bottom-tabs.note: Tab bar at the bottom of the screen

@react-navigation/drawer.note: Side menu that slides in from the edge

@react-navigation/elements.note: Shared UI pieces (headers, buttons) used by React Navigation

react-native-screens.note: Native screen containers; makes navigation faster (needed by React Navigation)

expo-router.note: File-based navigation: every file in app/ is a screen (built on React Navigation)

expo-linking.note: Open URLs and handle deep links into your app (myapp://...)

react-native-safe-area-context.note: Keeps content away from the notch, status bar and home bar

react-native-svg-transformer.note: Lets you import .svg files as components (set up in metro.config.js)

react-native-vector-icons.note: Icon fonts (Ionicons, MaterialIcons, ...); older all-in-one package

@react-native-vector-icons/common.note: Shared code for the @react-native-vector-icons/* icon font packages

@expo/vector-icons.note: Icon fonts (Ionicons, MaterialIcons, ...) that work in Expo Go

react-native-bootsplash.note: Native splash screen made from your logo; hide it from JS when the app is ready

nativewind.note: Style components with Tailwind CSS class names

expo-status-bar.note: <StatusBar /> component: light or dark status bar text

expo-font.note: Load custom fonts (useFonts) or embed them with its config plugin

expo-splash-screen.note: The splash screen: set it in app.json, keep it up while fonts and data load

expo-image.note: Fast <Image> with caching, placeholders and transitions

expo-system-ui.note: Sets the root background color and light/dark style of the native window

expo-symbols.note: Apple SF Symbols icons on iOS

react-native-reanimated.note: Smooth animations that run on the UI thread

react-native-worklets.note: Runs small JS functions on other threads (used by Reanimated)

react-native-gesture-handler.note: Native touch gestures: swipe, pan, pinch (used by drawers and sheets)

zustand.note: Small, simple global state (share data between screens)

@reduxjs/toolkit.note: Redux with less boilerplate: global state with slices

react-redux.note: Connects Redux state to React components

jotai.note: Global state built from small pieces called atoms

@tanstack/react-query.note: Fetches, caches and refreshes server data (loading/error states for you)

axios.note: HTTP client; an alternative to the built-in fetch()

expo-web-browser.note: Opens web pages in an in-app browser (also used for OAuth login)

expo-auth-session.note: Log in with OAuth providers (Google, GitHub, ...) through the browser

expo-updates.note: Over-the-air updates: ship JS changes without a store release (EAS Update)

react-hook-form.note: Form state and validation without lots of re-renders

zod.note: Describe the shape of data and validate it (forms, API responses)

@react-native-async-storage/async-storag.note: Save small key-value data on the device (not encrypted)

react-native-mmkv.note: Very fast key-value storage on the device

react-native-keychain.note: Store secrets (tokens, passwords) in the secure Keychain/Keystore

expo-secure-store.note: Store secrets (tokens) encrypted in the Keychain/Keystore

expo-sqlite.note: A SQLite database on the device

expo-file-system.note: Read, write and download files on the device

react-native-permissions.note: Ask for and check permissions (camera, location, ...)

react-native-device-info.note: Info about the device: model, OS version, app version

react-native-config.note: Read values from .env files in JS and native code

expo-constants.note: Read app.json values and app info at runtime (Constants.expoConfig)

expo-camera.note: Camera preview, photos, video and barcode scanning

expo-image-picker.note: Pick a photo from the library or take one with the camera

expo-location.note: The device's GPS location (asks for permission)

expo-device.note: Info about the device: model, OS, real device or simulator

expo-application.note: Info about the app: version, build number, bundle ID

expo-localization.note: The user's language, region and time zone

expo-sharing.note: Opens the share sheet for a file

expo-*.note: Expo module ({rest}); install it with `npx expo install expo-{rest}`

@babel/core.note: Babel compiler; Metro uses it to transform your code

@babel/preset-env.note: Babel settings for modern JavaScript syntax

@babel/runtime.note: Helper functions Babel adds to compiled code

@react-native/babel-preset.note: Babel settings that turn TypeScript/JSX into JavaScript for Metro

@react-native/metro-config.note: Default settings for Metro, the bundler that `npm start` runs

@react-native/typescript-config.note: Shared tsconfig settings for React Native projects

typescript.note: TypeScript compiler; `npx tsc` checks your types

babel-plugin-module-resolver.note: Import with short paths like '@/components/Button' (set up in babel.config.js)

babel-preset-expo.note: Babel settings for Expo projects (TypeScript, JSX, Reanimated, ...)

@react-native-community/cli.note: The `react-native` command: start, run-android, run-ios, doctor

@react-native-community/cli-platform-*.note: Adds {rest} commands to the CLI (`npm run {rest}`)

react-native-asset.note: Copies fonts and other assets into the android/ and ios/ projects (`npx react-native-asset`)

expo-dev-client.note: Your own version of Expo Go (a development build) that includes your native packages

expo-build-properties.note: Config plugin to set native build settings (SDK versions, ...) from app.json

@react-native/jest-preset.note: Jest settings that mock native code so tests run on your computer

react-test-renderer.note: Renders components in tests without a phone or simulator

@testing-library/react-native.note: Test components the way a user uses them (press, type, find text)

jest-expo.note: Jest settings for Expo projects (mocks the native modules)

eslint.note: Finds problems in your code (`npm run lint`)

eslint-config-expo.note: Expo's recommended ESLint rules (`npx expo lint`)

files.App.tsx: Root component: the first screen of your app is rendered from here
files.App.js: Root component: the first screen of your app is rendered from here
files.index.js: Entry point: registers App with AppRegistry so native code can start it
files.app.json: App name and display name used by the native projects
files.app.config.js: Expo config written as code: like app.json, but can read environment variables
files.app.config.ts: Expo config written as code: like app.json, but can read environment variables
files.eas.json: EAS Build and Submit profiles (development, preview, production): how cloud builds are made
files.expo-env.d.ts: TypeScript types for Expo, generated by Expo; don't edit it, and it isn't committed
files..expo: Expo's local cache and dev server settings; not committed
files.package.json: Lists your JS packages and npm scripts (npm start, npm run ios, ...)
files.package-lock.json: Exact versions npm installed; commit it so `npm ci` installs the same
files.yarn.lock: Exact versions Yarn installed; commit it (use only one package manager)
files.pnpm-lock.yaml: Exact versions pnpm installed; commit it (use only one package manager)
files.bun.lock: Exact versions Bun installed; commit it (use only one package manager)
files.bun.lockb: Exact versions Bun installed; commit it (use only one package manager)
files.node_modules: Installed JS packages for this project only; not committed, `npm ci` recreates it
files.android: Native Android project (Gradle); open this folder in Android Studio
files.ios: Native iOS project (Xcode + CocoaPods); open the .xcworkspace in Xcode
files.src: Your app code: screens, components, hooks, ...
files.assets: Images and fonts used by the app
files.patches: Fixes to packages in node_modules made with patch-package; applied after every install
files.babel.config.js: Babel settings: how your code is transformed before bundling
files.metro.config.js: Metro settings: the bundler that serves your JS to the app
files.react-native.config.js: React Native CLI settings: fonts and assets to link, autolinking exceptions
files..watchmanconfig: Settings for Watchman, the file watcher Metro uses
files.Gemfile: Ruby gems for this project, mainly the CocoaPods version iOS needs
files.Gemfile.lock: Exact Ruby gem versions; commit it
files..bundle: Bundler settings (installs gems into vendor/ for this project only)
files.vendor: Ruby gems installed by `bundle install` for this project only
files..nvmrc: Node version for this project; `nvm use` reads it
files..node-version: Node version for this project (read by fnm, Volta, nodenv, ...)
files..java-version: Java (JDK) version for this project, read by jenv or a shell hook
files..ruby-version: Ruby version for this project, read by rbenv/rvm
files..gitignore: Files git should not track (node_modules, build output, ...)
files..env: Environment values like API URLs; usually not committed
files.README.md: Notes about the project for you and your teammates
files..vscode: VS Code settings for this project

expoFiles.app.json: Expo config: app name, icon, splash screen, bundle ID / package name, plugins. Native folders are generated from it
expoFiles.android: Native Android project generated by `npx expo prebuild`; change native settings in app.json instead, prebuild rewrites it
expoFiles.ios: Native iOS project generated by `npx expo prebuild`; change native settings in app.json instead, prebuild rewrites it
expoFiles.app: Expo Router screens: every file is a route (app/index.tsx is /, app/settings.tsx is /settings)
expoFiles.assets: Images and fonts; app.json points at the icon and splash images in here
expoFiles.components: Reusable UI pieces used by your screens
expoFiles.hooks: Custom React hooks: reusable logic with state or effects
expoFiles.constants: Values used across the app, like colors (Colors.ts)
expoFiles.scripts: Helper scripts for package.json, like the template's reset-project.js
expoFiles.index.js: Entry point: registerRootComponent(App) starts your app
expoFiles.index.ts: Entry point: registerRootComponent(App) starts your app
expoFiles.metro.config.js: Metro settings, starting from Expo's defaults (expo/metro-config)
expoFiles.babel.config.js: Babel settings (babel-preset-expo): how your code is transformed before bundling

paths.android/app: The Android app module: its build.gradle, manifest, Kotlin code and resources
paths.android/app/build.gradle*: App build settings: package name (applicationId), version numbers, SDK versions, signing and release options
paths.android/build.gradle*: Project build settings shared by every module: SDK, NDK and Kotlin versions
paths.android/settings.gradle*: Lists the Gradle modules (:app) and plugs in React Native's Gradle plugin and autolinking
paths.android/gradle.properties: Gradle settings for the Android build: memory, New Architecture, Hermes, CPU architectures
paths.android/gradle: The Gradle wrapper: pins the Gradle version so everyone builds with the same one
paths.android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.pr: Which Gradle version ./gradlew downloads (distributionUrl); change it only when upgrading React Native
paths.android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.ja: The small program behind ./gradlew that downloads Gradle; commit it, don't edit it
paths.android/gradlew: Runs Gradle on macOS/Linux, e.g. `cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug`
paths.android/local.properties: This computer's Android SDK location (sdk.dir); not committed. Fixes 'SDK location not found'
paths.android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml: Declares the app to Android: permissions, the main activity, deep links, icon and label
paths.android/app/src/debug: Settings only used in debug builds
paths.android/app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xm: Debug-only manifest: allows plain HTTP so the app can reach Metro on your computer
paths.android/app/src/main/java: Your app's Kotlin/Java code (MainActivity, MainApplication), in folders named after the package
paths.android/app/src/main/java/**/MainApplica: Starts React Native when the app process starts: loads the native packages (autolinked) and the JS engine
paths.android/app/src/main/java/**/MainActivit: The one Android screen that shows your React Native app; getMainComponentName() must match the name in app.json
paths.android/app/src/main/res: Android resources: launcher icons (mipmap-*), the app name and theme (values/)
paths.android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-*: Launcher icons for one screen density (mdpi, hdpi, ... xxxhdpi); `rn-buddy app icon` makes them all from one image
paths.android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-*/*: A launcher icon image for this folder's screen density
paths.android/app/src/main/res/values: Strings, styles and colors of the native Android app
app_name: the name shown under the icon on Android (`rn-buddy app name` changes it)
paths.android/app/src/main/res/values/styles.x: The Android theme (AppTheme): window background, status bar and text field style before JS loads
paths.android/app/src/main/res/drawable: Images and XML shapes for the native side (splash screen, notification icons)
paths.android/app/src/main/res/drawable/rn_edi: The template's style fix for TextInput on Android; leave it as it is
paths.android/app/src/main/assets: Files packed into the app as they are, like fonts (fonts/)
paths.android/app/debug.keystore: The shared debug signing key every debug build uses. Never use it for a Play Store release
paths.android/app/*.keystore: A signing key. Keep release keys out of git and backed up: without it you can't update the app on Google Play
paths.android/app/proguard-rules.pro: Rules for R8/ProGuard, which shrinks release builds; libraries sometimes ask you to add keep rules here
paths.android/app/build: Build output; safe to delete (`rn-buddy clean --android`), never committed
paths.android/build: Build output; safe to delete (`rn-buddy clean --android`), never committed
paths.android/.gradle: Gradle's cache for this project; safe to delete, never committed
paths.android/.kotlin: Kotlin compiler cache; safe to delete, never committed
paths.android/app/.cxx: Native C++ build cache; safe to delete (`rn-buddy clean --android`), never committed
paths.android/link-assets-manifest.json: Written by react-native-asset: the fonts it linked; commit it so it can unlink them later
paths.ios/Podfile: The iOS native libraries (CocoaPods); autolinking adds your native packages. Run `(cd ios && bundle exec pod install)` after changes
paths.ios/Podfile.lock: Exact pod versions installed; commit it so everyone gets the same native libraries
paths.ios/Pods: Native iOS libraries installed by `pod install`; not committed, pod install recreates it
paths.ios/<app>: The iOS app target: AppDelegate, Info.plist, launch screen and images
paths.ios/<app>Tests: Native iOS unit tests (XCTest); safe to ignore while learning
paths.ios/<app>/AppDelegate.*: Starts the app on iOS: creates React Native and loads your JS (from Metro in debug, the bundle in release)
paths.ios/<app>/Info.plist: iOS app settings: display name, version, permission messages (NS...UsageDescription), allowed HTTP
paths.ios/<app>/LaunchScreen.storyboard: The launch screen iOS shows while the app starts; edit it in Xcode
paths.ios/<app>/Images.xcassets: iOS images, including the app icon (AppIcon) at every size
paths.ios/<app>/Images.xcassets/AppIcon.appico: The iOS app icon at every size; `rn-buddy app icon` fills it from one image
paths.ios/<app>/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy: Privacy manifest Apple requires: which 'required reason' APIs the app uses and what data it collects
paths.ios/<app>/*.entitlements: Capabilities such as push notifications, Sign in with Apple and app groups
paths.ios/<app>.xcodeproj: The Xcode project (targets, build settings). Don't open this one: open the .xcworkspace instead, or the pods are missing
paths.ios/<app>.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj: Xcode build settings: bundle ID, version, signing team. Change them in Xcode, not by hand
paths.ios/<app>.xcworkspace: Open this one in Xcode (`xed ios`): your app plus the Pods. Created by pod install
paths.ios/.xcode.env: Settings for Xcode's build scripts, mainly which node to use (NODE_BINARY); committed
paths.ios/.xcode.env.local: This computer's node path for Xcode, written by pod install; not committed. Fixes 'node: command not found' in Xcode
paths.ios/build: Build output; safe to delete (`rn-buddy clean --ios`), never committed
paths.ios/link-assets-manifest.json: Written by react-native-asset: the fonts it linked; commit it so it can unlink them later
paths.src/App.tsx: Root component: the first screen of your app is rendered from here
paths.src/App.js: Root component: the first screen of your app is rendered from here
paths.src/screens: One component per screen of the app: what the user sees after navigating somewhere
paths.src/components: Reusable UI pieces: buttons, cards, inputs, list items. Used by more than one screen
paths.src/navigation: Navigators: the list of screens and how the user moves between them (stack, tabs, drawer)
paths.src/hooks: Custom React hooks: reusable logic with state or effects. A hook's name starts with `use`
paths.src/services: Code that talks to the outside world: your API, storage, analytics. No React code here
paths.src/store: State shared between screens: the logged-in user, a cart, settings
paths.src/theme: Colors, spacing and font sizes in one place
paths.src/utils: Small helper functions: formatting, validation, calculations. No React and no network
paths.src/assets: Images and fonts bundled with the app
paths.src/assets/fonts: Font files (.ttf/.otf); they must be linked into the native projects before you can use them
paths.src/types: TypeScript types used by many files: API responses, app models
paths.src/features: One folder per feature (auth, profile, ...), each with its own screens, components and hooks
paths.src/features/*: One feature of the app: its screens, components, hooks and API calls together

expoPaths.app/**/_layout.*: Layout for the routes in this folder: wraps them in a Stack, Tabs or Drawer navigator (Expo Router)
expoPaths.app/**/(*): A route group: organizes screens (for example under a tab bar) without adding to the URL
expoPaths.app/**/+not-found.*: The screen shown when a link points to a route that doesn't exist
expoPaths.app/**/+html.*: Web only: the HTML page around your app
expoPaths.app/**/[*].*: A dynamic route: [id] in the name becomes a parameter (useLocalSearchParams)
expoPaths.app/**/index.*: The default screen of this folder's route
expoPaths.app/**/*.*: A screen: its file path is its URL in Expo Router (app/settings.tsx is /settings)
expoPaths.app/**/*: A folder of routes: its name becomes part of the URL

gradle.properties.org.gradle.jvmargs: Memory for the Gradle build. Raise -Xmx (e.g. -Xmx4096m) if builds fail with 'Java heap space' or 'Metaspace'
gradle.properties.org.gradle.parallel: Builds modules in parallel: faster builds
gradle.properties.org.gradle.daemon: Keeps a Gradle process running between builds so the next build starts faster
gradle.properties.org.gradle.caching: Reuses outputs of earlier builds: faster builds
gradle.properties.org.gradle.configureondemand: Only configures the modules a build needs
gradle.properties.android.useAndroidX: Uses AndroidX, the current Android support libraries. Keep it true
gradle.properties.android.enableJetifier: Converts old support-library packages to AndroidX; only needed for very old libraries
gradle.properties.android.enablePngCrunchInReleaseBuilds: Compresses PNG images in release builds
gradle.properties.reactNativeArchitectures: CPU types to build native code for. Keep only arm64-v8a (phones) and x86_64 (emulator) to build faster locally
gradle.properties.newArchEnabled: The New Architecture (Fabric, TurboModules). Required by recent React Native versions; every native library must support it
gradle.properties.hermesEnabled: Hermes, React Native's JS engine: faster startup and less memory. false means JavaScriptCore
gradle.properties.hermesV1Enabled: Uses the newer Hermes V1 engine
gradle.properties.edgeToEdgeEnabled: Draws the app behind the status bar and navigation bar (edge to edge). Use safe-area insets to keep content visible
gradle.properties.*_UPLOAD_STORE_FILE: Release signing: the keystore file (in android/app). Keep the real values out of git, in ~/.gradle/gradle.properties
gradle.properties.*_UPLOAD_KEY_ALIAS: Release signing: the key's name inside the keystore
gradle.properties.*_UPLOAD_STORE_PASSWORD: Release signing: the keystore password. Don't commit it; put it in ~/.gradle/gradle.properties
gradle.properties.*_UPLOAD_KEY_PASSWORD: Release signing: the key password. Don't commit it; put it in ~/.gradle/gradle.properties
gradle.properties.expo.*: Expo setting ({rest}), written by `npx expo prebuild` from app.json; change it there

gradle-wrapper.properties.distributionUrl: The Gradle version ./gradlew downloads. It must match the Android Gradle Plugin of your React Native version
gradle-wrapper.properties.distributionBase: Where the downloaded Gradle is stored (in ~/.gradle)
gradle-wrapper.properties.zipStoreBase: Where the downloaded Gradle zip is kept
gradle-wrapper.properties.zipStorePath: Folder for the downloaded Gradle zip
gradle-wrapper.properties.networkTimeout: How long (ms) to wait when downloading Gradle; raise it on a slow connection
gradle-wrapper.properties.validateDistributionUrl: Checks that distributionUrl is a valid Gradle download

build.gradle.namespace: The package of your Kotlin code (where R and BuildConfig live). Usually the same as applicationId
build.gradle.applicationId: The app's unique ID on Google Play (package name). It can't change after you publish: `rn-buddy app id` changes it
build.gradle.versionCode: Build number for Google Play: a whole number that must go up with every upload (`rn-buddy app version`)
build.gradle.versionName: The version users see, like 1.2.0 (`rn-buddy app version`)
build.gradle.minSdkVersion: The oldest Android version the app installs on (API level)
build.gradle.targetSdkVersion: The Android version the app is tested for; Google Play requires a recent one
build.gradle.compileSdk: The Android SDK version the app is compiled with
build.gradle.compileSdkVersion: The Android SDK version the app is compiled with
build.gradle.buildToolsVersion: Version of the Android build tools (installed with the SDK Manager)
build.gradle.ndkVersion: Version of the NDK used to build native C++ code; Android Studio installs it
build.gradle.kotlinVersion: Version of Kotlin used to build the native code
build.gradle.signingConfigs: The keys that sign the app. The template only has the debug key
build.gradle.signingConfig: Which key signs this build type. The template signs release builds with the debug key: change it before publishing
build.gradle.storeFile: The keystore file used for signing
build.gradle.enableProguardInReleaseBuilds: Shrinks and obfuscates release builds with R8. Smaller app, but test the release build: missing keep rules crash it
build.gradle.minifyEnabled: Turns R8 shrinking on or off for this build type
build.gradle.shrinkResources: Removes unused images and resources from release builds
build.gradle.proguardFiles: The R8/ProGuard rules files, including proguard-rules.pro
build.gradle.hermesEnabled: Picks the JS engine: Hermes when hermesEnabled=true in gradle.properties, otherwise JavaScriptCore
build.gradle.jscFlavor: The JavaScriptCore engine, used only when Hermes is turned off
build.gradle.autolinkLibrariesWithApp: Autolinking: adds the native code of your installed packages to the app
build.gradle.com.android.application: Gradle plugin that builds an Android app
build.gradle.com.facebook.react: React Native's Gradle plugin: bundles your JS, runs codegen and autolinking
build.gradle.com.facebook.react.rootproject: React Native's Gradle plugin, applied to the whole project
build.gradle.com.facebook.react:react-android: React Native itself (its version comes from node_modules/react-native)

Info.plist.CFBundleDisplayName: The name shown under the app icon (`rn-buddy app name` changes it)
Info.plist.CFBundleName: Short name of the app bundle; usually $(PRODUCT_NAME)
Info.plist.CFBundleIdentifier: The bundle ID, unique on the App Store. Usually $(PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER): the real value is in Xcode's build settings (`rn-buddy app id`)
Info.plist.CFBundleShortVersionString: The version users see, like 1.2.0. Usually $(MARKETING_VERSION) from Xcode (`rn-buddy app version`)
Info.plist.CFBundleVersion: Build number: must go up with every TestFlight upload. Usually $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)
Info.plist.CFBundleExecutable: Name of the app's executable; leave it
Info.plist.CFBundleInfoDictionaryVersion: Format version of this file; leave it
Info.plist.CFBundlePackageType: Kind of bundle (APPL = an app); leave it
Info.plist.CFBundleURLTypes: URL schemes that open your app (myapp://...), used for deep links and OAuth
Info.plist.LSRequiresIPhoneOS: The app runs on iOS; leave it
Info.plist.LSApplicationQueriesSchemes: Other apps' URL schemes your app may check with Linking.canOpenURL
Info.plist.NSAppTransportSecurity: Which plain-HTTP (not HTTPS) connections are allowed. NSAllowsLocalNetworking lets debug builds reach Metro; avoid NSAllowsArbitraryLoads in releases
Info.plist.NS*UsageDescription: The message iOS shows when the app asks for {rest} permission. Required before using it: the app crashes without it, and App Review rejects vague texts
Info.plist.UILaunchStoryboardName: The launch screen shown while the app starts (LaunchScreen.storyboard)
Info.plist.UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities: Device features the app needs to install (arm64 = any modern iPhone)
Info.plist.UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance: false lets React Native's <StatusBar> control the status bar
Info.plist.UIUserInterfaceStyle: Light, Dark or Automatic (follows the system setting)
Info.plist.UIAppFonts: Custom font files included in the app; a font must be listed here to work on iOS
Info.plist.UIBackgroundModes: What the app may keep doing in the background (audio, location, remote notifications)
Info.plist.UIFileSharingEnabled: Shows the app's Documents folder in the Files app
Info.plist.CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone: Allows 120 Hz animations on ProMotion iPhones
Info.plist.RCTNewArchEnabled: The New Architecture (Fabric, TurboModules) on iOS. Required by recent React Native versions
Info.plist.ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption: Export compliance: false (only standard HTTPS) skips the encryption question on every upload

app.json.name: The app's internal name: must match the name in AppRegistry.registerComponent and the native projects. Don't change it alone
app.json.displayName: The name used when the native projects were created. The name under the icon is in strings.xml and Info.plist (`rn-buddy app name`)
app.json.expo.name: The name shown under the app icon
app.json.expo.slug: URL-friendly name of the project on Expo's servers (EAS); don't change it after the first build
app.json.expo.owner: The Expo account or organization that owns the project
app.json.expo.runtimeVersion: Which native build an over-the-air update fits (EAS Update)
app.json.expo.orientation: Allowed screen orientation: portrait, landscape or default (both)
app.json.expo.icon: The app icon image (1024x1024 PNG); prebuild makes every size from it
app.json.expo.scheme: URL scheme for deep links (myapp://...); Expo Router and OAuth need it
app.json.expo.userInterfaceStyle: light, dark or automatic (follows the system setting)
app.json.expo.newArchEnabled: The New Architecture (Fabric, TurboModules); on by default in recent Expo SDKs
app.json.expo.jsEngine: The JS engine: hermes (default) or jsc
app.json.expo.splash: Splash screen image and background color (newer SDKs set it with the expo-splash-screen plugin)
app.json.expo.assetBundlePatterns: Which asset files are bundled into the app
app.json.expo.ios.bundleIdentifier: The iOS bundle ID, unique on the App Store (com.company.app)
app.json.expo.ios.buildNumber: iOS build number: must go up with every TestFlight upload
app.json.expo.ios.supportsTablet: Whether the app runs full screen on iPad
app.json.expo.ios.infoPlist: Extra Info.plist keys, like permission messages (NS...UsageDescription)
app.json.expo.ios.icon: A different app icon for iOS
app.json.expo.android.package: The Android package name, unique on Google Play (com.company.app); it can't change after you publish
app.json.expo.android.versionCode: Android build number: must go up with every Google Play upload
app.json.expo.android.adaptiveIcon: The Android icon in layers (foreground image + background color) so each phone can shape it
app.json.expo.android.permissions: Android permissions to add to AndroidManifest.xml
app.json.expo.android.blockedPermissions: Permissions to remove even if a library adds them
app.json.expo.android.edgeToEdgeEnabled: Draws the app behind the status and navigation bars (edge to edge)
app.json.expo.android.icon: A different app icon for Android
app.json.expo.web: Settings for the web version of the app
app.json.expo.plugins: Config plugins: they change the native projects for you when prebuild runs (permissions, fonts, SDK settings). Rebuild after changing them
app.json.expo.experiments.typedRoutes: Type-checks Expo Router links (href) against your app/ files
app.json.expo.experiments.reactCompiler: Turns on the React Compiler (automatic memoization)
app.json.expo.extra: Your own values, readable at runtime with Constants.expoConfig.extra
app.json.expo.sdkVersion: The Expo SDK version; normally taken from the expo package, leave it out
app.json.expo.platforms: Which platforms the app supports (ios, android, web)
app.json.expo.primaryColor: Main color used by Android for the app in the recent apps list
